Synopsis:
Debate between 2 BM patrons. One is trying to convince the other to skip a date and instead come back to the ship. Player can weigh in.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_Patron_01_Patron_09_Debate.json: The scene takes place in the Blushing Mermaid while the city — and the tavern’s patrons — are still on edge after recent threats and unmaskings; the party is preparing to ship out at first light. Siggy is worried and frustrated, urging her friend Svend to skip a date because violence could erupt before dawn; the narrator’s beat implies Siggy feels more for Svend than she lets on. Svend shrugs off the danger and plans to go anyway. The player can step in to back Siggy’s caution or mock/pressure Svend, and companions or other shaken survivors may be nearby but aren’t required to the exchange.
- CAMP_Karlach_CRD_ROM_Date.json: At camp, Karlach invites the player on a date. The dialogue will teleport them to the date location. If Henk is not available for the dialog, Honk will be instead.
- CAMP_Ravengard.json: Default Ravengard dialogue. Depending on the path, Ravengard may urge you to save the city, and if Wyll is in party, will offer the quest to go to the Wyrmway. Wyll's endgame state is detremined here: He may become a Duke, the Blade of Avernus, or remain the Blade of Frontiers
- LOW_SteelWatchFoundry_FundangoLosesHope.json: This dialog covers an edge case: the player has freed Iron throne prisoners, returned to the foundry and recruited Toobin as a follower. On the way to the control centre a kill switch accidentally goes off, killing all the gondians.Because of this Toobin is ready to give up. The player may attempt to persuade him to keep going.

But he knows where to listen, and has learned the location of the Stone Lord's ambush. We can learn it from him if we put up with his shit long enough.

context: The exchange takes place in the Blushing Mermaid while the city and tavern patrons are still on edge after recent threats and unmaskings, and the party is due to sail at first light. Siggy is frantic and frustrated, urging her friend Svend to skip a date because violence could erupt before dawn; the narrator suggests her concern is tinged with more-than-friend feelings. Svend shrugs off the danger and plans to go anyway. The player may step in to back Siggy’s caution or to mock/pressure Svend; other shaken survivors or companions might be nearby but aren’t required for the scene.
